title: A fully Gaussian quantum Stein's lemma
authors: Filippo Girardi, Jacopo Rizzo, Leah Turner, Gerardo Adesso, Ludovico Lami
abstract: A central yet mysterious problem in quantum information is the asymptotic distinguishability of quantum states under restricted measurements. Here we look at asymptotic asymmetric hypothesis testing for general multi-mode bosonic Gaussian states restricted to arbitrary collective Gaussian measurements. We establish a single-letter formula for the Stein exponent for many pairs of states, featuring two distinct contributions, corresponding to first and second moments, respectively. Remarkably, the Gaussian-measured relative entropy exhibits genuine non-additivity, but the only effect of additivity violations is to asymptotically decouple first and second moments. We prove this by establishing sufficient conditions for additivity of the second-moment term via novel log-determinant matrix inequalities. Our results not only identify a single-letter expression for the Gaussian Stein exponent in a wide range of practical situations, but also rule out any possible advantage from collective Gaussian measurements when considering centred Gaussian states.
summary: This paper derives a single-letter formula for the Gaussian Stein exponent, which quantifies the asymptotic distinguishability of multi-mode bosonic Gaussian states. It proves that this exponent separates into independent contributions from the first and second moments. The results establish conditions under which collective measurements do not provide an asymptotic advantage over optimized single-copy measurements.
main_problem: The paper investigates the asymptotic distinguishability of multi-mode bosonic Gaussian quantum states under restricted collective Gaussian measurements.
main_result: The Gaussian Stein exponent factorizes into independent first-moment and second-moment contributions, and additivity of the covariance term is established under specific structural conditions on the covariance matrices.
method: The analysis uses asymptotic limits ($n 	o \infty$) and techniques involving log-determinant matrix inequalities and symplectic geometry to characterize the rate of distinguishability.
model_or_system: The system involves multi-mode bosonic Gaussian states, characterized by their first moments (displacements) and quantum covariance matrices (QCMs). The testing framework uses collective Gaussian measurements.
key_observables: Gaussian Stein exponent ($	ext{Stein}_G$), Gaussian-measured relative entropy ($D_G$), and the error probabilities ($\alpha_n,  eta_n$).
important_parameters: The number of copies ($n$), the covariance matrices ($V, W$), and the displacement vectors ($s, t$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on asymptotic limits ($n 	o \infty$) and establishing sufficient conditions for additivity based on the structure of the covariance matrices.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the Umegaki relative entropy, the classical Wigner relative entropy upper bound, and the Gaussian Stein exponent for discriminating between a vacuum and a thermal single-mode state.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the factorization of the Stein exponent into moment contributions. It then analyzes the additivity of the covariance term, providing sufficient conditions (Theorem 2/7) for this additivity. Finally, it derives the single-letter expression for the exponent, showing the separation of the two moment contributions.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, single-letter formula for a key measure of distinguishability in bosonic quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding the limits of quantum communication and sensing protocols.
